title: Shortest Subarray With Sum at Least K
statement: You are given an integer array nums (values may be negative, zero, or positive) and an integer k. Consider every non-empty contiguous subarray of nums. Return the length of the shortest such subarray whose elements sum to at least k (that is, sum >= k). If no non-empty contiguous subarray reaches a sum of k, return -1. Because the array may contain negative numbers, a plain expanding/shrinking window is not valid here: the running sum is not monotonic across window edges, so a shorter qualifying subarray can begin after a dip that an ordinary sliding window would have already discarded.
hints: Rewrite sum(i..j) >= k as a difference of two cumulative totals, one at each endpoint, so any subarray sum is a single subtraction. For a fixed end position, what lets you find the best start quickly?
Sweep the prefix array with a deque of candidate start indices kept in increasing prefix-value order; a smaller-and-later prefix always dominates a larger-and-earlier one, so pop those from the back.

For each j: while the front start satisfies prefix[j] - prefix[front] >= k, record j - front and pop the front (it can never give a shorter answer again); then pop from the back while prefix[back] >= prefix[j] before appending j. Answer is the smallest length seen, else -1.
